title: Staged drain reservations and rolling upgrade orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a fleet-level orchestrator that performs staged node drains and rolling upgrades while guaranteeing throughput reservations and minimizing tail-latency impact for Dedicated capacity customers. The orchestrator will coordinate with autoscaling policies, pre-reservation tokens, and the KV/prefix cache layer to ensure in-flight requests are served and that latency SLOs are respected during maintenance windows and upgrades.

Goals:
- Provide an automated rolling upgrade and maintenance mechanism that preserves throughput guarantees for customers with reserved capacity.
- Implement staged drain behavior: honor existing work queues and KV cache affinity, but evict new work with configurable prioritization to accelerate safe drains.
- Coordinate with autoscaler to avoid rapid scale-downs during maintenance and to allow temporary burst capacity when needed.
- Expose controls in the Console and API for maintenance windows, reservation sizing, and drain policies (e.g., fast/standard/conservative).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change scheduler placement heuristics or introduce new hardware affinity policies beyond stage-aware KV-cache hints. Those are follow-ups.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Maintenance reservation token: when a maintenance window is scheduled for a pool, the orchestrator calculates a temporary throughput reservation (percentage of pool) that must remain available to honor customer reserved capacity. This is derived from per-route SLOs and active commitments.
2) Staged drain phases:
   - Pre-drain (T-2h default): Mark target node(s) as maintenance_preparing; sync KV cache eviction hints to neighbors. Pause new long-running batches from being scheduled to the node.
   - Soft-drain (T-30m default): Deprioritize new requests to the node (route to healthy nodes or to a lower-priority queue). Allow in-flight requests to finish unless they exceed per-request deadline.
   - Hard-drain (start of maintenance): Evict remaining tasks using a prioritized eviction policy (preserve high-SLA tokens), and signal autoscaler to spin temporary burst nodes if pool headroom insufficient.
3) Autoscaler coordination:
   - During pre-drain and soft-drain phases, autoscaler is annotated not to aggressively scale down.
   - If hard-drain would breach throughput reservation, orchestrator requests a short-lived burst from Dedicated capacity autoscaling (documented and billable).
4) KV cache awareness:
   - Drain policy includes KV-cache affinity hints. Before hard-drain, attempt to warm neighbor nodes with top-K prefixes observed on the draining node to reduce cold-start token cost.
5) Rollout and rollback:
   - Canary upgrades on a small percentage of nodes in non-peak hours. If tail-latency or error rate increases beyond threshold, orchestrator halts rollout and executes rollback to previous model/runtime image.

API/Console surface:
- New Maintenance API endpoints: scheduleMaintenance(pool_id, start, end, drain_policy, reservation_pct) and listMaintenance(pool_id).
- Console UI: maintenance timeline with expected throughput reservation, estimated customer impact, and allow manual override.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Cluster tests: run rolling upgrade across a dedicated pool while sustaining 95% of committed throughput for 99% of time during maintenance window in synthetic traffic tests.
- Latency SLOs: end-to-end p95 must not regress by more than 10% from baseline during staged drain in standard mode.
- KV warmup: warmup reduces cold-token generation rate on neighbor nodes by >=30% within 10 minutes in experiments.
- Autoscaler: orchestrator requests temporary burst nodes when reservation_pct would be violated; verify billing metrics emitted and autoscaler honors request.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will implement orchestrator as a control-plane service integrated with fleet-controller. This keeps logic outside runtime path but requires reliable control-plane scaling.
- KV warmup trades cost for latency: warming neighbors increases short-term token processing but reduces long-tail latency. We will make warmup configurable per-customer.
- Reservation sizing heuristic: conservative default (10% buffer) but allow customers to set explicit reservation_pct.

Observability and alerts:
- Dashboard tile per-pool showing maintenance events, reservation usage, eviction rates, and KV-cache warmup progress.
- Alerts: maintenance-failed-to-reserve-capacity, maintenance-rollback-triggered (reasons), maintenance-excess-eviction (more than X evictions/min).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for state transitions and API validation.
- Integration tests with simulator that reproduces request placement, KV cache distribution, and autoscaler interaction.
- Canary cluster run with traffic mirroring of a real customer workload for 24h before enabling full rollout.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind dedicated-fleet-maintenance-v2.
2) Deploy orchestrator to control-plane in canary region.
3) Run internal pools through maintenance windows for 2 weeks and collect metrics.
4) Gradual opt-in for customers; default to existing drain behavior unless they opt in.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: control-plane failure mid-maintenance could leave nodes in drained state. Mitigation: idempotent state machine and fallback to manual override UI with guardrails.
- Risk: autoscaler overspends on burst; mitigation: hard budget threshold and an approval flow for large bursts.
- Risk: KV warmup inefficacy across heterogenous workloads; mitigation: make warmup advisory and allow customers to disable.
